name: Contracts
description: Register of CDAs, MSAs, SOWs and other agreements with key dates and obligations: contract families with total value, notice and expiry alarms, obligations owed by and to the company, a CDA check, a pre-signature pipeline and a due-diligence list. Signed originals are TrialAgents documents; Claude or ChatGPT proposes terms with quotes and a person verifies them.
whenToUse: A small biotech needs one register of its agreements (CDAs, MSAs, SOWs, change orders, MTAs, licences, CMO supply, quality, consulting, clinical trial, data processing and lease agreements) with families, key dates, notice deadlines, obligations, CDAs and reminders, with signed originals stored in TrialAgents and assistant extraction verified by a person.
whenNotToUse: Drafting or negotiating contract language, clause libraries, redlining, approval chains, e-signature, legal review or risk scoring, procurement, purchase orders and invoice matching (Trial Finance), and employment contracts.

heading.description: App heading shown above every screen.

tableMap.description: JSON object keyed by stable role key: core data contract v1 roles agreements and organizations (required) and people, programs, studies (optional); app roles contracts.settings, contracts.terms, contracts.obligations (output, contract contracts.v1); integration programs.plan_items (programs.v2): this app's own milestone entries, or Programs' plan items (read only) once the user links Programs inside the app. Each value is {typeId:<authorized table UUID>, fields:{<logical key>:<real field key>}, writableFields:[<logical keys>]}. Real keys are lowercase snake_case.

pageSize.description: Rows per page in registers, 10–50; the template clamps the value.

layoutProfile.description: JSON presentation profile written only by native layout settings through a reviewed, versioned app update.

readOnly.description: When true, the app proposes no writes even for users who may edit.

demoLabel.description: Label the app as a fictional demo. Only for the repository preview.

asOfOverride.description: Optional fixed as-of date (YYYY-MM-DD) for previews and tests only. Leave empty: the app uses today's date from the app runtime.

instructions:
Contracts 1.1.0 is a custom frontend-js contract register that follows docs/product/MODULAR_APPS_AND_SHARED_DATA.md: shared tables use core data contract v1 role keys (agreements, organizations, people, programs, studies), app tables use contracts.* role keys, contracts.obligations is a published output (contract contracts.v2, a superset of contracts.v1, writer life.contracts), programs.plan_items is an integration with Programs, features that use another app's data degrade gracefully, and removing an app or tab never deletes data. Contracts tracks agreements; it does not draft or sign them.

1. Discover and pin. Read read_app_template_guidance (usage; authoring when extending; contracts for the role registry) to the last nextOffset, read_app_design, list_app_templates and read_app_template for life.contracts. Pin this exact version and digest and keep one requestKey for the creation.
2. Install and reuse. Before installing, call list_archived_items (kind apps, this templateId) and offer to restore an archived Contracts app first. Use shows the Use existing data? dialog: an existing agreements table (for example Runway's) and organizations table are connected by default, and the seven Contracts-owned optional agreements fields (parent_id, program_id, study_id, total_value, currency, signed_on, owner) are added to it in the same installation. people, programs and studies connect when present, otherwise Contracts gets its own tables. When Programs is installed, its plan items are offered for programs.plan_items (read only); otherwise Contracts keeps its own milestone entries. You may propose choices with prepare_data_access; only the user confirms. Never seed demo data.
3. Map fields. Core roles use exactly the core data contract v1 fields; never rename, retype or remove them. agreement_type and status stay text fields in the core contract; Contracts writes only the documented option values. Only Contracts writes the Contracts-owned agreements fields. Use multiple:false, lowercase snake_case real keys and scalar record-ID text for relationships (counterparty_id, parent_id, program_id, study_id, agreement_id, milestone_id).
4. Two ways in, both chosen by the user; nothing is read automatically. (a) The user gives you a contract, or names an original already uploaded in Contracts: upload it as a TrialAgents document if it is not one yet (platform upload review), read it with list_documents and read_document_text (follow hasMore) only if it is AI-readable, and store the agreement, its key terms and its obligations in one reviewed change (step 5). If an original is not listed for you, say it is not readable and ask the owner to make it AI-readable in Documents; never guess its contents. (b) The user uploads the original in the app and types the details in, or leaves them blank; blank terms are fine.
5. Filling in from a contract. One reviewed prepare_change batch: the agreements record if it is missing (name, agreement_type, counterparty_id, status, effective_date, expiry_date, signed_on, total_value, currency, parent_id when it is a SOW or change order of a known MSA); then, once its receipt ID exists, contracts.terms {agreement_id, renewal, renewal_term_months, notice_days, confidentiality_years, cda_direction, purpose, governing_law, document_id, document_version_id, extraction_status:"proposed", source_quotes: JSON {field:{quote,page}}} and contracts.obligations {agreement_id, counterparty_id (the agreement's counterparty unless the contract names another party), title, kind, direction, due_date or trigger, recurrence, milestone_id, amount, currency, owner, status:"open", verified:false, source_quote (the exact sentence), source_page, source_document_version_id}. Do not calculate the app's dates yourself: the app calculates notice deadline and confidentiality end from these fields and stores them on its next save. Quote exactly and flag uncertainty. Proposals stay "not checked" until checked: by a person in the app (Verify proposals, each quote checked against the extracted text), or by you when the user explicitly asks, through the review (verified true; on terms extraction_status verified, verified_by the user's name, verified_on today).
6. Everything in the app is yours to change within the access the user gave you; every write goes through the TrialAgents review. Each button is an exact record change you can make with prepare_change: Add or edit (create or update the record from its form fields); Archive (archived true); Add child agreement (agreement with parent_id); Move status in Pipeline (agreements.status; contracts.terms.status_since today); Mark signed (status active, signed_on, effective_date, expiry_date; status_since); Mark done / waived / missed (contracts.obligations.status); Renewal decision (a line "Renewal decision on <date>: renew|renegotiate|terminate — note." appended to contracts.terms.notes; renegotiate also sets agreements.status in_negotiation and status_since); New CDA (agreement type cda_nda, status drafting; then terms with cda_direction and purpose); Settings (the one contracts.settings row: default_currency, reminder_days, agreement_types, obligation_kinds); Attach an original (contracts.terms document_id and document_version_id, or document_link). Read-only features answer from the same records with the rules in documentation.dataContract: Overview, Families (family value per currency), CDAs ("do we have a CDA with X?": agreements of type cda_nda for that organization with direction and confidentiality end), Due-diligence list, Obligations calendar ("what do we owe CRO Y?": open obligations, checked first; label unchecked ones). Draft renewal decision notes and the due-diligence list on request. Never give legal advice or risk opinions, draft or negotiate contract language, or send documents.
7. Customization. Layout uses the native gear (tracker:layout → prepare_tool_layout). Forms are generated from the logical schema S in the source (field key, label, kind text/longtext/number/date/select/boolean/person/ref, options, required) and the tableMap: to add a field, add it to the table with a reviewed schema change and, in one reviewed app revision, add it to S and to that role's tableMap fields and bindings; it then appears in the form, the details panel and validation. Fields bound but not in S are shown read-only under "Additional fields". New forms, screens, charts or features are reviewed app revisions; build forms on the same S entries, valuesFromForm validation and records.propose path. Keep: role keys and contracts, the calculation rules, the "From <App>" labels of read-only connected values, data-ui-state and stable data-action on inputs. Revise the same saved app; preserve IDs, bindings and access.
8. No automations. Contracts has no recommended automations and no scheduled work; the Overview, Obligations, CDAs and Pipeline screens show deadlines and pending agreements on demand. The user may add their own automations later in TrialAgents → Automations.

quickStart: Read the current usage, authoring and contracts guidance and this template's documentation; pin life.contracts 1.1.0 and its digest with one requestKey.

Settings → Add organization for each counterparty (or reuse the shared organizations). Optionally edit settings: agreement types, obligation kinds, reminder windows (30, 60, 90 days) and default currency.
Add a contract: give it to Claude or ChatGPT to store with its terms and obligations, or Register → Add agreement / Upload the original and type the details in (blank is fine).
Check assistant-filled entries: open the agreement → Verify proposals, or ask the assistant to mark them checked through the review.
Add SOWs and change orders with Add child agreement; track CDAs in CDAs and agreements before signature in Pipeline.
documentation.dataContract: Stable role keys. Core data contract v1: agreements (name text*, counterparty_id text record ID of organizations, agreement_type text with values cda_nda/msa/sow_work_order/change_order/mta/research_collaboration/licence_in/licence_out/cmo_supply/quality_agreement/consulting_advisory/clinical_trial_agreement/data_processing/lease_services/other, status text with values drafting/in_negotiation/out_for_signature/active/expired/terminated/superseded, effective_date date, expiry_date date, archived boolean; Contracts-owned optional fields parent_id text record ID of the master agreement, program_id, study_id, total_value money, currency select USD/EUR/GBP/CHF/CAD/AUD/JPY/CNY/SEK/DKK/NOK/INR, signed_on date, owner text), organizations (name*, org_type, country, website, archived), and optional people, programs, studies (core fields). App tables (contracts.v1): contracts.settings (one row: default_currency, reminder_days comma list default 30,60,90, agreement_types and obligation_kinds comma lists of enabled values in order); contracts.terms (one per agreement: agreement_id text*, renewal select none/automatic/option, renewal_term_months, notice_days, notice_deadline date calculated by the app, confidentiality_years, confidentiality_end date calculated by the app, cda_direction select mutual/incoming/outgoing, purpose, governing_law, document_id, document_version_id, document_link URL text, extraction_status select none/proposed/verified, source_quotes JSON text {field:{quote,page}}, verified_by text, verified_on date, status_since date, notes). Output contracts.obligations (contracts.v2, a superset of contracts.v1, writer life.contracts): agreement_id*, counterparty_id text record ID of organizations (defaults to the agreement's counterparty), title*, kind* payment/report/diligence_milestone/notice/delivery/publication_review/audit/insurance/royalty/other, direction* we_owe/they_owe, due_date, recurrence none/monthly/quarterly/annual, trigger, milestone_id record ID of programs.plan_items, amount money, currency, owner, status* open/done/waived/missed, verified boolean, source_quote, source_page number, source_document_version_id, archived. Integration programs.plan_items (programs.v2; name, program_id, item_type, end_date, status, is_key): Contracts' own milestone entries until the user links Programs in the app, then Programs' plan items read only. Calculations: notice_deadline = expiry_date − notice_days when renewal is automatic or option; confidentiality_end = (expiry_date, or effective_date without expiry) + confidentiality_years × 12 calendar months, day clamped to the month end; family value = master total_value + Σ children per currency, other currencies listed separately and never converted, change-order share = Σ change orders ÷ family value in the master's currency; earliest expiry and next notice over active members; next due of a recurring obligation = first occurrence on or after the as-of date; expires before milestone = active agreement whose program has a key milestone after its expiry. Calculated by the app from the fields whenever it shows them, whoever saved the record; stored copies of notice_deadline and confidentiality_end are refreshed on the app's next save and are used only when the inputs are missing. Unverified (not yet checked) = obligations with verified false or terms with extraction_status proposed; never counted as confirmed. Values read from another connected app are labelled From <App> and are changed in that app. Every field is scalar multiple:false; relationships are record IDs. Reads are bounded to 800 rows per table; partial reads disable totals and say so. Signed originals are TrialAgents documents with their own permissions and AI-readable flag. Access is app-level; database column rules can hide total_value and amount.
documentation.interactionContract: Seven screens with stable IDs for the native layout gear: overview, register, families, obligations, cdas, pipeline, settings; column groups agreements and obligations. Overview: next deadline sentence (“Cancel X by 1 Dec 2026 or it renews for 12 months”), counts per reminder window, the next 90 days (expiries, notice deadlines, verified obligations due, CDA confidentiality ends), needs attention (overdue obligations, unverified extractions, agreements that expire before a key milestone), agreements by type and status, and in-flight agreements with days in status. Register: search over the register and optionally the signed originals (documents.search, with coverage), filters (type, counterparty, program, status, verification, expiry window), paging, Add agreement, Upload the original (data-trialy-document upload button: the platform upload review), Due-diligence list (filters for types, statuses and a minimum value; copyable Markdown), and a side panel with key terms, renewal decision, signed original (AI-readable and extraction status, upload or attach), family, obligations with quotes, counterparty contacts and record history. Families: collapsible tree per master with family value per currency, change-order share, earliest expiry, next notice and Add child agreement. Obligations: table with next due, verified status, Mark done/waived/missed and Verify (all reviewed), a 12-month calendar and payments by month and currency. CDAs: “Have we signed a CDA with…?” check, new CDA request (counterparty and purpose, status drafting), CDAs by organization and confidentiality ending within a year. Pipeline: three columns (drafting, in negotiation, out for signature) with owner and days in status, reviewed moves and Mark signed (dates, then the prompt to upload the signed original). Settings: reviewed settings row, milestones (own entries, or From Programs read only, with the subtle Add Programs / Use its milestones line), counterparties, access and automation pointers. Details panels label values from another connected app From <App> and show bound fields this version does not know under Additional fields (read only). Verify proposals: proposed values with quotes and pages, each checked against the extracted text (documents.quote), a decision per obligation (verify, leave, reject) and the verifier's name; one reviewed batch. Every input carries data-ui-state and a stable data-action; drafts survive failed proposals; record versions are captured when an editor or confirmation opens; at most 50 writes per review. No app login, browser storage or network calls.
documentation.lifecycle: New previews show fictional or empty data and never read documents or write. Saved apps re-read their tables and configuration on every render; layout changes are reviewed app revisions; record writes are records.propose batches confirmed in the TrialAgents review, and a stale version is rejected with the draft kept. A new agreement's starting key terms are offered as a follow-up save once the agreement has its record ID. Uploading an original is a platform review with explicit confirmation; the app then learns the new version ID and offers to attach it. An assistant fills in a contract only when the user asks; its entries stay not checked until a person verifies them in the app, or the assistant does on the user's explicit request, both through the review with the name and date recorded. Archiving hides records but keeps them and their history; removing the app or a tab never deletes data; an archived app is restored with its data and its automations switched off. Linking Programs is a one-time choice in the in-app integration dialog; after that the milestones are read only and Contracts' own entries stay in Database.
limitations: No drafting, templates, clause library, redlining, negotiation workflow, approval chains or e-signature; no legal advice or risk scores. Contracts tracks agreements; it does not sign them.

Filling in from a contract is done by the user's connected assistant (Claude or ChatGPT) on request, not by the app or on a schedule; only AI-readable originals can be read, and scanned originals need text extraction to finish first.
Amounts in different currencies are never converted or summed together.
Days in status are known only for status changes made in Contracts (status_since); older agreements show “unknown”.
Reads are bounded to 800 rows per table and 200 document versions; partial reads disable totals and say so.
Values from another connected app (for example Programs milestones) are read only here and are changed in that app; Contracts cannot open the other app directly.
Fields added to a table in Database after install appear read-only under Additional fields; ask the assistant to add them to the forms.

examples.prompt: Here is the signed Corvane supply agreement. Store it in Contracts.
examples.expectedBehavior: Uploads the original as a TrialAgents document through the upload review, reads its text, and proposes one reviewed batch: the agreement, contracts.terms (extraction_status proposed, source quotes with pages) and obligations (verified false, counterparty, exact source_quote and source_page). Leaves the dates the app calculates to the app and says the entries can be checked in Contracts or by asking.

examples.prompt: I uploaded the Brightwater DPA in Contracts. Fill in its terms.
examples.expectedBehavior: Finds the AI-readable original attached to that agreement, reads it and proposes the terms and obligations as one reviewed change. If the original is not readable for the assistant, it says so and points to Documents instead of guessing.

examples.prompt: Have we signed a CDA with Northwind Bio?
examples.expectedBehavior: Reads agreements of type cda_nda for that organization and answers with the agreement, direction (mutual), status, signature date and confidentiality end (1 Mar 2032 in the fictional demo).

examples.prompt: Add a 'Budget code' field to obligations and show it in the form.
examples.expectedBehavior: Prepares the reviewed schema change adding budget_code (text) to the obligations table, then one reviewed app revision adding it to S.obligations and to the obligations tableMap and binding; the field appears in the obligation form and details. Explains both reviews.

examples.prompt: We do not want any automations.
examples.expectedBehavior: Nothing to change: Contracts installs with no automation. The Overview, Obligations, CDAs and Pipeline screens give the same information on demand.

tasks.whenUseful: Contracts declares no automations and needs none: deadlines, obligations due, CDA confidentiality ends and agreements waiting for signature are shown on Overview, Obligations, CDAs and Pipeline. Filling in a contract is done on request by the user's connected assistant.
tasks.promptExample: Show me what needs action in Contracts this week.
